exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $75,810.00 as of 2026-11-05 17:42:52 UTC, +0.56% over one hour and -5.48% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $75,573.00 to $80,882.00; spot sits at 5% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -6.52% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($79,850.35) is above the 72-hour average ($78,251.51). Spot is 6.61% below the seven-day high of $81,172.94 and 0.31% above the seven-day low of $75,573.00.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.33% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 8.3, conventionally oversold.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $39.32 billion, equal to 2.58% of the $1.52 trillion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 50 ("Neutral"), versus 51 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink BTC/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $76,169.53, 40 minutes before the spot quote and +0.47% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of $75,810 sits near the bottom 5% of the 24‑hour range ($75,573‑$80,882) indicating a clear price floor and ample upside to the range ceiling, a classic set‑up for a bullish reversal [Ex. B, A].  

2. Despite a –6.52% seven‑day decline, the 24‑hour average ($79,850) already exceeds the 72‑hour average ($78,251), showing accelerating buying pressure, while the RSI of 8.3 flags a deep oversold condition that historically precedes rapid rebounds [Ex. C, D].  

3. Liquidity remains robust at $39.32 billion (2.58% of market cap), and the Chainlink feed—our settlement reference—quotes $76,169, a 0.47% premium to spot, confirming market makers are willing to pay above current levels, reinforcing upward bias [Ex. E, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is perched near the low end of its 24‑hour range (5% above the floor) while the 14‑hour RSI of 8.3 signals extreme oversold conditions, indicating strong upside potential if buyers step in [Ex. B, D].  

2. Despite a 6.52% seven‑day decline, the 24‑hour average ($79,850.35) already exceeds the 72‑hour average ($78,251.51), showing short‑term buying pressure that is likely to lift the price toward the recent high of $81,172.94 [Ex. C].  

3. Liquidity remains robust with $39.32 billion traded in the past day, providing ample depth for a short‑term rally, and the Chainlink feed—our settlement benchmark—shows a 0.47% premium to the spot quote, reinforcing a modest upward bias for the next 24 hours [Ex. E, G].  

For these reasons the Bear respectfully requests that the Court open a SHORT practice position.  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point collapses under the reality of the 24‑hour range: the price sits merely 5 % above the floor, yet the high of $80,882 remains 5 % above current levels, indicating a wide gap that buyers must bridge—no guarantee of “strong upside” from an oversold RSI alone [Ex. B, D].  

Second, the Bear’s claim of short‑term buying pressure is hollow because the seven‑day decline of 6.52 % dwarfs the modest 24‑hour average advantage; the 24‑hour average merely sits 1.6 % above the 72‑hour average, a marginal edge insufficient to reverse a multi‑day downtrend [Ex. C].  

Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first premise collapses on the very range it cites: spot sits only 5 % above the low, not near a “floor,” because the 24‑hour low equals the seven‑day low, showing no true support and leaving the ceiling barely 6 % higher – an insufficient upside to justify a reversal [Ex. B, C].  

Second, the Bull misreads momentum: an RSI of 8.3 is oversold, but realized volatility of 2.33 % per day signals a lethargic market lacking the explosive buying needed for a bounce, especially when the seven‑day trend remains –6.52 % and the Fear & Greed Index is merely neutral at 50, not bullish [Ex. D, C, F].  

Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds that the evidence favors a short practice position for BTC/USD over the next 24 hours.

findings.finding: Spot price is $75,810, only 5% above the 24‑hour low, indicating limited upside.
RSI of 8.3 shows extreme oversold conditions while realized volatility is low at 2.33% per day, suggesting weak buying momentum.
Seven‑day trend remains negative at –6.52% despite a modest 24‑hour average edge, confirming continued bearish pressure.

ruling.opinion: The Court notes that BTC trades near the bottom of its recent range (Ex. A, B) and the seven‑day decline persists (Ex. C). Although the RSI is oversold (Ex. D), the low realized volatility indicates insufficient thrust for a reversal. Neutral sentiment (Ex. F) and modest volume (Ex. E) provide no bullish catalyst, and the Chainlink premium (Ex. G) is too small to offset downside bias. Consequently, a short position is warranted.
ruling.dissent: The dissent argues that the extreme oversold RSI and the Chainlink premium signal a potential rebound that could justify a long position.
